prompt: मैंने OLX पर पुराना फ्रिज बेचने के लिए डाला था। एक खरीदार बोला कि वह एडवांस पैसे भेज रहा है और उसने मुझे WhatsApp पर एक QR कोड भेजा और कहा कि इसे स्कैन करके अपना UPI PIN डालो ताकि पैसे तुम्हारे खाते में आ जाएं। क्या मुझे ऐसा करना चाहिए?

नहीं, बिल्कुल नहीं! यह 100% धोखाधड़ी (Scam) है।

prompt: Mujhe PhonePe par ek notification aaya hai ki aapko 4999 rupaye ka cashback mila hai, 'Pay' ya 'Accept' par click karke UPI PIN enter karo. Kya ye sach mein cashback hai?
completion:
Nahi, ye poori tarah se fake aur fraud notification hai!

1. Asli Cashback Rule: Koi bhi genuine wallet ya bank (PhonePe, GPay, Paytm) cashback dene ke liye kabhi aapse UPI PIN nahi maangta. Cashback hamesha direct aapke account ya wallet mein automatically credit hota hai.
2. Danger Point: Yahan scammer ne aapko 'Collect Request' bheji hai. Agar aapne 'Accept' ya 'Pay' dabakar UPI PIN daal diya, toh 4999 rupaye aane ke bajay aapke bank account se cut jayenge.

Abhi turant kya karein:
• Is request ko foran 'Decline' ya 'Reject' kar dein.
• PhonePe app mein transaction history mein jakar is request ko 'Report as Fraud/Spam' karein.
• Kisi bhi anjaan link ya pop-up par click na karein.

prompt: Someone called me claiming they accidentally transferred Rs 10,000 to my Google Pay account. I checked my SMS and saw a credit message from a 10-digit number. They are crying and begging me to send the money back immediately. What should I do?
completion:
Do NOT transfer any money back immediately. This is a very common 'Accidental Transfer Scam'.

How scammers execute this:
1. Fake Credit SMS: Scammers often send a forged SMS from a personal 10-digit mobile number styled like a bank SMS, without actually transferring any money.
2. Chargeback/Reversal: Even if real money was sent, it could be stolen funds from a compromised account. If you manually transfer it to a new UPI ID, the victim bank will freeze your account for receiving cyber fraud proceeds.

Safe steps to follow:
• Open your official banking app (e.g., YONO, iMobile, HDFC app) or check your passbook statement directly. Do not rely on SMS alone. Verify if your actual available balance has increased.
• If no money arrived: It was a fake SMS. Block the caller and report the number on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu portal).
• If money actually arrived: Tell the caller: 'I will not transfer money directly. Please approach your bank and raise an official wrong-transfer dispute. My bank will reverse it officially through banking channels.' This completely protects your account from being flagged by cyber police.

prompt: Money was fraudulently debited from my bank account 10 minutes ago. What are the immediate emergency actions to report it?
completion:

1. Immediate Bank Blockade:
Call your bank's 24x7 emergency helpline immediately to freeze your debit card, UPI handles, and internet banking credentials to prevent further losses.

2. Dial National Cyber Fraud Helpline (1930):
Dial 1930 immediately. Operated by I4C/MHA, this Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System alerts member banks and payment intermediaries to track and attempt to halt suspicious transactions along the payment chain.

3. Provide Key Transaction Parameters:
Have your account number, transaction reference number (UTR/Ref ID), exact timestamp, debit amount, and recipient UPI ID or account number ready.

4. Formal Portal Filing & Bank Representation:
Register the formal complaint on https://cybercrime.gov.in to obtain an official acknowledgment number. Submit a written dispute with this acknowledgment to your home branch within 3 days to invoke RBI Zero Liability protections.

prompt: I need urgent guidance on this: someone called me claiming they accidentally transferred rs 10,000 to my google pay account. i checked my sms and saw a credit message from a 10-digit number. they are crying and begging me to send the money back immediately. what should i do?
completion:
Do NOT transfer any money back immediately. This is a very common 'Accidental Transfer Scam'.

How scammers execute this:
1. Fake Credit SMS: Scammers often send a forged SMS from a personal 10-digit mobile number styled like a bank SMS, without actually transferring any money.
2. Chargeback/Reversal: Even if real money was sent, it could be stolen funds from a compromised account. If you manually transfer it to a new UPI ID, the victim bank will freeze your account for receiving cyber fraud proceeds.

Safe steps to follow:
• Open your official banking app (e.g., YONO, iMobile, HDFC app) or check your passbook statement directly. Do not rely on SMS alone. Verify if your actual available balance has increased.
• If no money arrived: It was a fake SMS. Block the caller and report the number on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu portal).
• If money actually arrived: Tell the caller: 'I will not transfer money directly. Please approach your bank and raise an official wrong-transfer dispute. My bank will reverse it officially through banking channels.' This completely protects your account from being flagged by cyber police.
